# Sberbank (SBRCY) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 025 | Published 2020-07-05 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-7-5/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/025.json)

Dollar funding relief and Russian bank value.

Sberbank's domestic profitability thesis had support; the investor-access risk overwhelmed a simple low-multiple valuation. The ruble five-year base case missed, while the explicit sanctions warning was borne out. Remaining ADR holders received a nonzero liquidation entitlement in 2026, so calling the position universally worthless would also be wrong. International-equity decade forecasts remain open, with unfavorable five-year relative evidence.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

### 025-C02

**Claims imply large worker churn**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | US employment |
| Source blocks | 23, 26, 27, 30, 34, 35 |
| Thesis family | ui-claims-persons-confusion |

Simultaneous hiring and layoffs are plausible, but claims count benefit weeks and may include backlogs. Comparing those directly to establishment payroll jobs also mixes persons, jobs and coverage; the text acknowledges a mismatch but not its full measurement cause.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [COVID-19 oversight report](https://files.gao.gov/reports/GAO-21-265/index.html) | GAO | 2021-01-28 | Verified in the audit

GAO found continued-claim totals counted weeks, not unique beneficiaries. DOL clarified this in December 2020; backlogs could produce several weeks per person in one report.

- [Pandemic impact on May employment statistics](https://www.bls.gov/covid19/employment-situation-covid19-faq-may-2020.htm) | Bureau of Labor Statistics | 2020-06-05 | Verified in the audit

The misclassification discussed concerned household-survey labor-force status. Establishment payrolls count workers paid for any part of the reference pay period, even when absent; unpaid absentees are excluded.

### 025-C04

**Dollar debts create funding squeezes**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Offshore dollars |
| Source blocks | 38, 39, 40 |
| Thesis family | dollar-em-debt |

The Federal Reserve documented severe offshore dollar-funding pressure in March 2020 and the relieving role of central-bank facilities. Trade receipts are one funding source, not the only way borrowers can service dollar liabilities.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Financial Stability Report: funding risk](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/may-2021-funding-risk.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2021-05-06 | Verified in the audit

March 2020 global dollar funding pressures increased as wholesale funding contracted and hedging/credit-line demand rose. Swap-funded auctions helped foreign banks meet commitments and build liquid assets without selling dollar assets.

- [June 2020 Monetary Policy Report, part 2](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/2020-06-mpr-part2.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-06-12 | Verified in the audit

Investors sold longer Treasuries and MBS for liquid assets; Treasury bid-ask spreads widened and dealer balance-sheet constraints impaired intermediation. Purchases and lending aimed to restore market function.

### 025-C23

**Small positions contain tail losses**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Portfolio |
| Source blocks | 141 |
| Thesis family | position-size-tail-risk |

For an unlevered standalone sleeve, its loss cannot exceed its invested capital. This is a bounded portfolio identity, not evidence that a basket of cheap countries must have positive expected returns.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Portfolio loss contribution is position weight times asset loss, absent leverage or correlated additional exposures.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- Unlevered position paid in full
- No additional capital commitment, recourse liability or short exposure
- Asset value cannot fall below zero

At weight w, value can decline from w times initial portfolio capital to zero. Direct loss is at most w times initial capital. Correlated losses elsewhere remain separate.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

**Next test:** Reconstruct entry, actual pre-2022 ADR payouts, custody, conversion and liquidation entitlement; do not extend a terminated ADR to 2029.

**Outcome evidence:**

Remaining ADRs became rights to $4.476211 net liquidation proceeds. Underlying sale required a 70% discount to March 13, 2026 MOEX close; mandatory cancellation, reconciliation and holder eligibility matter.

The broad follow-on relief act was signed in December, later than the summer/pre-election expectation. Interim executive unemployment assistance existed, so a total absence of summer support would overstate the miss. Equities rose and the dollar fell in the summer, but the proposed legislative catalyst cannot be credited for that timing.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.
